FOREWORD
0.4 l'his standard is one of the two Indian Standard Specifications for Processed Barley. The other specification is IS: 1157-1957 Barley Powder. 0.5 This standard requires reference to the following Indian Standard Specifications:
265-1950 HYDROCHLORIC ACID 266-1950 SULPHURIC ACID 460..1953 TEST SIEVES 1070-1957 DISTILLED WATER 0.5.1 Wherever a reference to any specification IS: IS: IS: IS:

G.l This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 21 November 1957, on approval by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council of the draft finalized on 23 September 1957, by the Edible Starches, Confectionery and Cereal Products Sectional Committee. 0.2 Pearl barley is manufactured by gradual abrasing of the husk and then the outer portion of the barley. kernel - the abrasing (popularly kno\vn as pearling) continued till the grains become rounded or pearly and get polished so that the endospenn is as \vhite as po~sible. Pearl barley should be made from well-filled barley, devoid of �discoloured or shrivelled kernels and of
foreign matter or other grains. 0.3 'The Sectional Committee responsible for the preparation of this standard has based it on the actual data available on the composition of pearl barley as manufactured in India from both imported as \vell as indigenous barley. Nevertheless, due weightage has also been given to the need for co-ordination between the standards prevailing in various c.Quntries. l"'his consideration led the Sectional Committee to refer to US Federal Specification No. N-B-I21, dated 26 October 1950, for Barley, Pearl. In addition to the above, due consideration has also been given to the relevant rules prescribed by the (;ovenlment of India under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. Still, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under that Act, wherever applicable.

mentioned under 0.5 appears in this standard, except IS: 460-1953 it shall be taken as a reference to the latest version of the specification. 0.6 The (iovernment of India have decided to introduce throughout the country uniform weights and measur~s based on the metric system. Therefore, the quantities in this standard have been given in metric units. 0.7 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS: 2-1949 Rules for Rounding Off Numerical Values; the number of places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as those of the specified value in the standard. 0.8 This standard is intended chiefly to cover the technical provisions relating to the supply of the material, and .it does not include all the necessary provisions of a contract. .

1. SCOPE
1.1 'Ihis standard prescribes the requirements and the methotis of test for pearl barley.

2. SAMPLING 2.1 Representative samples of the material shall l)e dra\vn according to the method prescribed� in Appendix _A. 3. REQ'UIREMENTS 3.1 The material shall be nian~factured essentially from sound and clean barley' ( HM'deum~ vulgare). It shall be whitish in colour and shall'be free from fermented, musty or other objectionable taste andodour, facings (mineral or otllerwiSe) and adulterants.
The colour, taste and -odour shaD be deter~ mined by organoleptic tests.
NOTE -

3.2 Barley-Grain Content - When examined by the method given in Appendix B, the barleygrain content shall be not less than 98�9 percent by weight. Matter other than barley shall have not nl()re than 1�0 percent by weight of "food grains other than barley" - and not. more than 0�1 percent by weight of cc foreign matter." 3.2.1 Damaged G,ains - When detennined by the method given in Appendix B, the total quantity of -grains damaged by heat, insects, moulds or other disease shall be not more than 2�0 percen~ by we.ight. .
3.3 The material shall also conform tQ the requiremen-~s given in Table.!.
a~ prescribed under 3.1 and in the appropriate appendices .specified-under 3.2, 3.2.1 and "in col 4 c:'f Table 1.-

4.2 Quality of Reagents 4.2.1 Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals
shall be employed in tests, and distilled water (see IS: 1070-1957) shall be used where the use of water as a reagent is intended.
NOTE - ' Pure chemicals' shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities which affect the results of analysis.

APPENDIX A (Cla'ltse 2.1 )
SAMPLING OF PEARL BARLEY

A-I. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS OF
SAMP~NG

A-I.O In drawing, preparing, storing and handling samples, the follo\\,ing precautions and directions shall be observed. A-I.I Samples shall be taken in a protected place not exposed to damp air, dust or soot. A-I.l The sampling instrument shall be clean and dry when used. A-I.3 Precautions shall be taken to protect the samples. the material being sampled, the sampling instrument and the containers for samples from adventitious contamination. ~".1.4 The sample':4.) shall be placed in clean and dry glass containers. The sample containers �shall be of such a size that they are almost completely filled by the sample. A-l.5 Each container shall be sealed air-tight after filling and marked with full details of sampling, date of sampling, batch or code number, name' of the manufacturer and other important parti~ulars of the consignment. 3

A-l.6 Samples shall be stored in such a manner that the temperature of the material does not vary unduly from the normal temperature. A~::1.7 Sampling shall be done by a person agreed bet\\'ccn the purchaser and the vendor and in the presence of the purchaser (or his representative) and the vendor ( or his representative ).
A~2. SCALE OF SAMPLING
A~2.1 Lot - All the containers in a single consignment of the Inaterial drawn from a single batell of manufacture shall constitute a lot. If the COllsignment is declared to consist of different batches of manufacture, the batches shall be Illarked separately and the groups of containers in each batch shall constitute separate lots. A-2.2 Gross Sample - For the purpose of dra\\ing samples for test, a number of containers shall be selected at random from a lot. This number of containers in relation to the size of the lot, or the scale of sampling, shall be subject to an agreement between the purchaser and the vendor. As a guide to such an agreement, a scale of the size of the sample is suggested in Table II.

A-3.2 Three sets of test samples, each sample being not less than 250 g shall be transferred immediately to thoroughly clean and dry containers and sealed air-tight. This shall be labelled with particulars given under A-I.5. One set of test samples shall be sent to the purchaser and one to the vendor. A-3.3 Referee Sample - The third set of test samples, bearing seals of the purchaser and the vendor, shall constitute the referee sample, to be used in case of dispute between the purchaser and the vendor. It shall be kept at a place agreed between the purchaser and the vendor.

A-4. TEST FOR ACCEPTANCE A-4.1 Examination and Tests - The purchaser may examine and test each of the reduced samples
constituting a test sample separately for compliance with the requirements of this standard or he may prepare, for the purpose of such examination and at any stage of the progress of the examination, a composite sample representative of the whole lot, by mixing all the reduced samples constituting the test sample.

A-3. TEST SAMPLES AND

REFEREE SAMPLE
A-3.! Preparation - To prepare a set of test samples, draw with an appropriate sampling instrument from different parts of each container in the gross sample, about 0�75 kg of the material and mix thoroughly to form a composite sample of that container. Divide the composite .sample of each container into three equal parts; each part shall form a reduced sample for that container. A set of such reduced samples, consisting of the reduced sample from each container shall constitute the test sample.

A-4.2 Criterion fo~ Judgement - When the individual reduced samples in a test sample are separately examined and the results vary from one reduced sample to another, the criterion for judging the quality of the lot for the purpose of acceptance on the basis of the results obtained shall be at the discretion of the purchaser, unless otherwise previously agreed between the purchaser and the vendor.

APPENDIX B (Clauses 3.2 and 3.2.1 )
DETERMINATION OF BARLEY-GRAIN CONTENT B-1. PROCEDURE
B-l.l Weigh accurately about 100 g of the material. Spread it out on a large sheet of paper. Pick out, using a forceps, � food grains other than barley', foreign matter (see 3.2) and damaged grain kernels (see 3.2.1) and form three separate groups. Weigh each group accurately.

B-2. CALCULATION
B-2.1 Percent by weight, of each group

= weight in g of the group, and WI = weight in g of the material taken for the test. B-2.2 Barley-grain content = 100 - ( percent ( food grains other than barley' percent foreign matter).

APPENDIX C [Table I, Item (i)]
DETERMINATION OF MOISTURE

C-l. PROCEDURE

C-l.1 Preparation of Sample - Grind in a
l)estle and mortar about 100 g of the material

so that at least 90 percent passes through IS Sieve 40 (ASA Test Sieve 40, BS Test Sieve 36 or Tyler Test Sieve 35). Transfer this p,epared sample to a well stoppered glass bottle

IS : 1156 - 1957 for use as indicated under e-l.2, F-3.1, G-2.!

and B-2.1.
C-I.l Weigh accurately about 5 g of the prepared sample in a dish made of porcelain, silica or platinum, previously dried in an electric oven and weighed. Place the dish in an electric oven maintained at 10s o �1�C, for five hours. Cool the dish in a desiccator and weigh with the lid on. Repeat the process of heating, cooling and weighing at half hour intervals until the loss in weight bet\veen two successive weighings is less than one milligram. Record the lowest weight ohtained.

NOTE - Preserve the dish containing this dried material for the determination of total ash (see D-l.l ).

APPENDIX F [Table I, Item (iv)]
DETERMINATION OF PROTEIN
F-l. APPARATUS
Transfer quantitatively to the round bottom Bask, with water, the total quantity of water used being about 200 ml. Add with shaking a few pieces of pumice stone to prevent bumping. Add about SO ml of sodium hydroxide solution ( \vhich is sufficient to make the solution alkaline) carefully through the side of the flask so that it does not mix at once with the acid solution but forms a layer below the acid layer. Assemble the apparatus taking care that the tip of condenser extends belo,,, the surface of standard sulphuric acid contained in the beaker. Mix the contents of the flask by shaking and distil until all ammonia has passed over into the standard sulphuric acid. Shut off the burner and immediately detach the flask from the condenser. Rinse the condenser thoroughly with water into the beaker. Wash the tip carefully so that all traces of the condensate are transferred to the beaker. When all the \vashings have drained into the beaker, add t\\�o or three drops of methyl red indicator solution and titrate with standard sodium hydroxide solution.

F-l.l KJeldahl Flask - 500 rol capacity.

� F-l.2 Distillation Assembly - The assembly
consists of a round bottom flask of 1 000 ml capacity fitted with a rubber stopper through which passes Dne end of the connecting bulb tube. The other end of the bulb tube is connected to the condenser which is attached by means of a rubber tube to a dip tube which dips into a known quantity of standard sulphuric acid contained in a beaker of 250 ml capacity.

F-2. REAGENTS
F-2.0 The follo\ving reagents are required.

F-2.1 Anhydrous Sodium Sulphate F-2.2 Copper Sulphate F-2.3 Concentrated Sulphurl~ Acid sp-gr 1�84 (see 15:266-1950). F-2.4 Sodium Hydroxide Solution - Dissolve about 225 g of s.odium hydroxide in 500 ml of
water.

F-3.2 Carry out a blank determination using all reagents in the same quantities hut without the material to be tested. F-4. CALCULATION F-4.1 Protein
(on dry basis), 87 500 (B-A )N percent by weIght = U'( lOO-M ) where B = volume in rol of standard sodium hydroxide solution used to neutralize the acid in the blank determination, A = volume in ml of standard sodium hydroxide solution used to neutralize the excess of acid in the test with the material, N = normality of the standard sodium hydroxide solution, W weight in g of the material taken for the test, and M moisture, percent by weight, in the material (see 0-2.1 ).

F-l.5 Standard Sulphuric Acid - approximately 0�1 N. F-l.6 Methyl Red Indicator Solution - Dissolve one gram of methyl red in 200 ml of rectified spirit ( 9S percent by volume). F-l.7 Standard Sodium Hydroxide Solutionapproximately 0�1 N.
